material_systems.name: DTM Acrylic Primer for Steel / Iron

primer.type: Direct-to-metal acrylic primer — UV stable, flexible, flash-rust resistant
products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer
Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec DTM Acrylic Primer
primer.notes: Standard primer for carbon steel and wrought iron. UV stable — tolerates longer recoat windows than epoxy. Flexible acrylic binder resists cracking from thermal expansion. Flash-rust inhibitors prevent rust bloom during drying in humid conditions. Coverage on smooth steel at high end (500 SF/gal); pitted/corroded steel at low end (400 SF/gal). Spray or brush application. Single coat standard — two coats on heavily pitted surfaces where first coat fills profile.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for ferrous metals. Preferred over DTM alkyd for long-term flexibility and UV stability. DTM acrylic does not require solvent cleanup — water-based. Compatible with all acrylic topcoats. NOT for galvanized or aluminum — lacks etch adhesion chemistry for slick non-ferrous surfaces.

material_systems.name: DTM Alkyd Primer for Steel / Iron (Alternative)

primer.type: Direct-to-metal alkyd primer — superior wetting and penetration into pitted surfaces
products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Alkyd Primer
primer.notes: Alternative primer for carbon steel and wrought iron. Superior wetting and penetration into pitted/corroded surfaces — alkyd binder flows into microscopic pits better than acrylic. Becomes brittle over time — not ideal for substrates with high thermal cycling. Solvent-based — requires mineral spirits cleanup. BLOCKED on galvanized (saponification — zinc oxide is alkaline, hydrolyzes alkyd binder). BLOCKED on aluminum (insufficient flexibility for aluminum's thermal expansion coefficient).

material_systems.notes: Best choice for heavily pitted steel where wetting is critical. Long-term brittleness makes it secondary to DTM acrylic for general use. HARD BLOCK on galvanized and aluminum substrates — see compatibility rules COMPAT-METL-001 and COMPAT-METL-003.

material_systems.name: Zinc-Rich Primer for Critical Steel (QT5 Only)

primer.type: High zinc-dust content galvanic (sacrificial) primer — cathodic protection
primer.notes: Specialty primer providing galvanic (sacrificial) protection — zinc corrodes preferentially to protect underlying steel. High zinc dust content (65-85% by weight in dry film). Requires near-white blast cleaning (SSPC-SP10 / NACE 2) for proper adhesion and galvanic contact. Very low coverage due to high solids content and thick film requirement. QT5 ONLY — cost, surface prep requirement, and application skill level exceed QT3/QT4 scope. Topcoat required — zinc-rich primer alone is not UV stable.

material_systems.notes: Premium corrosion protection for critical steel elements — structural columns, exposed beams, high-value ornamental iron. Carbon steel only — galvanized already has zinc coating, aluminum does not corrode galvanically with zinc. Requires specialty surface prep (blast cleaning) not available in standard residential painting scope. Specialty product — may require special ordering.

material_systems.name: Surface-Tolerant Epoxy Primer

primer.type: Two-component surface-tolerant epoxy primer — excellent adhesion on marginal prep
primer.notes: Surface-tolerant epoxy for marginal prep situations where blast cleaning or full mechanical prep is impractical (intricate ornamental work, occupied-adjacent areas). Two-component mix — limited pot life (4-8 hrs depending on temperature). NO UV RESISTANCE — must topcoat within recoat window (24-72 hrs depending on product). Chalks and degrades rapidly if left exposed. Excellent chemical resistance and adhesion. Best for situations where aggressive surface prep is not feasible.

material_systems.notes: Specialty primer for difficult conditions. Two-component product requires careful mixing and has limited pot life. CRITICAL: Must be topcoated within manufacturer's recoat window (typically 24-72 hrs) — epoxy chalks and loses adhesion if exposed to UV beyond window. Not for galvanized or aluminum — etch primer is the correct choice for those substrates.

material_systems.name: Etch / Wash Primer for Galvanized and Aluminum

primer.type: Phosphoric acid etch primer (wash primer) — microscopically etches slick non-ferrous surfaces
products: Sherwin-Williams Wash Primer (vinyl butyral / phosphoric acid)
primer.notes: Etch primer for galvanized steel and aluminum. Phosphoric acid component microscopically etches slick zinc/aluminum oxide surfaces to create mechanical adhesion profile. Vinyl butyral binder provides corrosion inhibition. Very thin film — acts as adhesion promoter rather than barrier coat. For galvanized: T-wash (mordant solution) is an alternative pre-treatment. Must be topcoated — etch primer alone provides no UV or weather protection. DFT: 0.3-0.5 mils (much thinner than DTM primers at 2-4 mils).

material_systems.notes: REQUIRED primer for galvanized and aluminum substrates. Standard DTM primers (acrylic or alkyd) will not adhere to slick zinc oxide or aluminum oxide surfaces. Etch primer creates the adhesion profile that enables topcoat adhesion. Very thin film — does not fill surface irregularities. May be followed by DTM acrylic primer for additional build on rough profiles.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Surfaces

primer.type: High-adhesion acrylic bonding primer for slick and factory-finished metal surfaces
products: Benjamin Moore Stix Waterborne Bonding Primer
primer.notes: Bonding primer for factory-finished or slick metal surfaces where etch chemistry is not appropriate (e.g., intact factory powder coat or baked enamel that needs color change, not bare metal). Acrylic resin with superior adhesion promoters. Water-based — easy cleanup. Does not etch surface — relies on resin adhesion chemistry. Alternative to etch primer when substrate is not bare metal. Good for aluminum gutters/downspouts with intact factory finish.

material_systems.notes: Use when the existing factory finish is intact and the goal is color change or refresh — not when bare metal is exposed. On bare galvanized or aluminum, use SYS_EXT_METL_PRIMER_ETCH instead. Bonding primer over intact factory finish avoids the need for aggressive mechanical prep on thin-gauge aluminum (which risks distortion).

material_systems.name: DTM Acrylic Exterior Finish for All Metal Substrates

finish.type: Direct-to-metal 100% acrylic exterior finish — UV stable, flexible, corrosion resistant
products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec DTM Acrylic Enamel
PPG Pitt-Tech Plus DTM Industrial Enamel
finish.notes: Standard topcoat for ALL metal substrates after appropriate primer. DTM acrylic enamel provides hard, durable finish with excellent UV resistance and color retention. Semi-gloss and gloss standard for metal — higher sheen improves moisture shedding and cleanability on exterior metal. Two coats at all quality tiers for metal (single coat on metal shows holidays and thin spots on convex profiles). Water-based — easy cleanup, low VOC. Compatible with all primer systems in this spec.

material_systems.notes: Universal finish for exterior metal. Semi-gloss is standard residential; gloss for ornamental and high-visibility elements. Metal finish must be DTM-rated — standard exterior house paint lacks the hardness and adhesion required for metal substrates. Coverage is for smooth metal — pitted or textured surfaces will consume more material. Two coats mandatory at all tiers — metal holiday coverage requires two passes.

material_systems.name: Rust Conversion Treatment

specialty.type: Phosphoric/tannic acid rust conversion product — converts iron oxide to stable iron phosphate/tannate
specialty.notes: NOT a primer — must be primed after conversion. Converts unstable red iron oxide (rust) to stable black iron phosphate/tannate compound. Used on surface rust in intricate areas where full mechanical removal is impractical (ornamental ironwork details, hard-to-reach crevices). Application: brush or spray onto rusted surface after loose rust removal. Allow 24-48 hrs cure to black. Surface must be primed after conversion — converter alone provides 1-3 year corrosion protection only. Do NOT use on structural rust (material loss) — conversion cannot restore section loss.

material_systems.notes: Supplementary treatment — not a replacement for mechanical rust removal on accessible surfaces. Best for intricate ornamental details where wire brushing cannot reach all crevices. Must be followed by primer + finish system. Chemical converts existing rust but does not prevent new rust — primer/finish system provides ongoing protection.

smooth_steel.notes: Clean smooth steel — minimal porosity, maximum coverage.

pitted_steel.notes: Pitted or lightly corroded steel after mechanical prep — pits consume additional material.

wrought_iron_ornamental.notes: Ornamental wrought iron — complex profiles (pickets, scrolls, rosettes) with many edges and corners. Effective coverage lower due to geometry.

assumptions: Coverage is per coat for brush application on the stated surface condition.
Spray on narrow profiles (railings, pickets) has 25-30% overspray waste — reflected in spray modifier.
Spray_backbrush recovers some overspray by working it into surface — slightly better than spray-only.

smooth_steel.notes: Clean smooth steel. Alkyd wets better than acrylic but slightly lower coverage due to higher solids.

pitted_steel.notes: Pitted/corroded steel — alkyd excels here due to superior wetting and penetration into pits.

assumptions: Coverage is per coat for brush application.
Alkyd has higher solids content than acrylic — slightly lower coverage but better wetting on pitted surfaces.
Spray waste similar to acrylic on narrow profiles.

blast_cleaned_steel.notes: Near-white blast cleaned steel (SSPC-SP10). Very low coverage due to high zinc dust solids content and thick DFT requirement (3-4 mils).

assumptions: Zinc-rich primer is typically spray-applied for even film build. Brush is for touch-up only.
Coverage is extremely low — budget 4-5 gallons per 1000 SF.
QT5 only — specialty product with specialty application requirements.

marginal_prep_steel.notes: Surface-tolerant epoxy on hand/power tool cleaned steel (SSPC-SP2/SP3). Coverage moderate — thick film build for barrier protection.

assumptions: Two-component product — factor in pot life waste (unused mixed material at end of pot life).
Coverage per coat. Single coat standard at 4-6 mils DFT.
Must be topcoated within recoat window — do not overestimate application pace.

galvanized_surface.notes: Galvanized surface — very thin film (0.3-0.5 mils). High coverage per gallon but only acts as adhesion promoter.

aluminum_surface.notes: Aluminum surface — similar thin film. Slightly lower than galvanized due to aluminum oxide hardness.

assumptions: Etch primer is extremely thin — high coverage per gallon but provides no barrier protection alone.
Must be topcoated with DTM acrylic finish system.
Spray overspray on etch primer is lower than on thicker primers due to thin film.

factory_finished_metal.notes: Factory-finished or intact previously painted metal. Smooth surface — good coverage.

assumptions: Coverage on intact factory finish — smooth, non-porous surface.
If factory finish is peeling/failing, additional prep reduces effective coverage.

railing_lf.notes: Railing: ~1-2 SF per LF (both sides of pickets + top/bottom rails). Midpoint 1.5 SF/LF. Complex baluster profiles at high end.

gutter_lf.notes: Gutter: ~0.5-1.0 SF per LF (exterior face only — interior not typically painted). Smooth profile, good coverage.

downspout_lf.notes: Downspout: ~0.3-0.5 SF per LF (circumference of round/rectangular profile). Small surface area per LF.

ornamental_ea.notes: Ornamental iron elements (scrollwork, rosettes, finials) — EA measurement. Complex geometry reduces effective coverage. Significant brush detail work.

flat_panel_sf.notes: Flat metal panels (column wraps, fascia covers) — direct SF measurement. Smooth surface, highest coverage.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two coats at all quality tiers — multiply material by 2x for total.
LF-to-SF conversion factors provided for railing, gutter, downspout profiles.
Spray waste on narrow metal profiles (railings, downspouts) is significant — 25-30% overspray on small targets.
Spray_backbrush recovers some overspray and ensures full film build on all sides of profiles.
Ornamental iron has highest waste due to complex geometry — many edges, corners, and recesses.

surface_rust_area.notes: Coverage depends on rust depth and porosity. Heavy surface rust at low end, light surface rust at high end.

assumptions: Applied only to rusted areas — not full surface area.
Coverage per application. Single application standard — heavy rust may require second application.
Cure time 24-48 hrs before priming — schedule accordingly.

consumables.name: Angular sash brush 2 inch (metal detail)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 200 LF of railing/gutter/downspout brushed
consumables.notes: Primary brush for metal painting. Angular sash cuts into tight profiles — picket-to-rail junctions, gutter lips, downspout seams. Nylon/polyester blend for water-based DTM acrylic. Natural bristle (china bristle) for alkyd DTM. 2 inch is standard — small enough for detail, wide enough for production.

consumables.name: Angular sash brush 3 inch (metal field)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 300 LF of flat runs brushed
consumables.notes: Wider brush for flat runs — gutter faces, flat railing top rails, metal panel field areas. Faster production than 2 inch on straight runs. Same bristle selection rules as 2 inch.

consumables.name: Detail / artist brush 1-2 inch (QT5 ornamental)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 50 EA ornamental details touched up
consumables.notes: Small detail brush for QT5 ornamental ironwork — scrollwork crevices, rosette petals, finial tips. Pointed tip for precision. QT5 only — QT3/QT4 do not require this level of detail finishing.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 411 (narrow fan for metal profiles)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 30 GAL material sprayed
consumables.notes: Small fan pattern (8 inch wide) with 0.011 orifice for narrow metal profiles — railings, downspouts, pickets. Narrow fan minimizes overspray on small targets. For acrylic DTM primer and finish.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 515 (medium fan for gutters and panels)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 35 GAL material sprayed
consumables.notes: Medium fan pattern (10 inch wide) with 0.015 orifice for wider metal surfaces — gutter runs, flat panels, wide rails. Faster production than 411 on linear runs.

consumables.name: Wire brush (hand — carbon steel bristles)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 100 LF of hand wire brushing
consumables.notes: Hand wire brush for loose rust, mill scale, and flaking paint removal (SSPC-SP2 hand tool cleaning). Carbon steel bristles for ferrous metals. Stainless steel bristles REQUIRED for aluminum and galvanized — carbon steel bristles leave iron deposits that cause galvanic corrosion on non-ferrous metals.

consumables.name: Wire wheel / grinding disc for angle grinder (power tool prep)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 200 LF of power tool cleaning
consumables.notes: Wire wheel or knotted wire cup brush attachment for angle grinder. SSPC-SP3 power tool cleaning — removes tight rust, mill scale, and failing paint faster than hand methods. Same bristle material rules: carbon steel for ferrous, stainless steel for non-ferrous. Grinding disc (36-80 grit) for heavy rust scale removal on flat surfaces.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80-120 grit (metal surface profile)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 SHEET per 25 SF sanding
consumables.notes: For scuff sanding previously painted metal surfaces to create adhesion profile. 80 grit for heavy mill scale or thick old paint. 120 grit for general scuffing of intact paint. Also used for feathering edges where old paint has chipped.

consumables.name: Scotch-Brite abrasive pads (maroon — medium)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 50 LF of hand sanding on metal profiles
consumables.notes: Non-woven abrasive pads for scuff-sanding contoured metal surfaces where sandpaper cannot conform — curved railings, round downspouts, ornamental profiles. Maroon (medium) grade provides adequate adhesion profile without excessive material removal on thin-gauge metals.

consumables.name: Mineral spirits / denatured alcohol (SP 1 solvent clean)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 QT per 200 LF of solvent wipe cleaning
consumables.notes: SSPC-SP1 solvent cleaning — remove oil, grease, and contaminants BEFORE mechanical prep. Critical first step — grinding over oil drives contamination into surface profile. Mineral spirits for general degreasing. Denatured alcohol for galvanized and aluminum (avoids residue). Apply with clean rags, wipe until rag shows clean.

consumables.name: Clean wiping cloths / rags
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA (bag of 25) per 500 LF of solvent wiping
consumables.notes: Lint-free wiping cloths for solvent cleaning step. MUST be clean — reusing contaminated rags redistributes grease. White rags preferred so contamination is visible. Dispose of solvent-soaked rags in fire-safe container (spontaneous combustion risk with mineral spirits).

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade, UV-resistant)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL per 30 EA fixtures or junctions masked
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. For masking adjacent non-metal surfaces at metal-to-wood, metal-to-masonry junctions. Also for masking hardware, address plates, mailbox slots.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting for overspray protection (2-4 mil)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL per 200 SF coverage area
consumables.notes: Plastic sheeting for protecting adjacent surfaces from spray overspray. Critical for metal spray work — narrow profiles generate significant overspray drift. 2 mil for temporary single-day cover. 4 mil UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. Secure with tape or weights.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 100 SF ground coverage below work area
consumables.notes: Canvas drop cloths for catching drips and overspray beneath railings, gutters, and downspouts. Non-slip for crew safety. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking paper (kraft, 12-18 inch wide)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL per 100 LF of adjacent surface masked
consumables.notes: Kraft masking paper for protecting siding, trim, and masonry adjacent to metal elements being sprayed. Applied with painter's tape. Critical for spray applications on gutters/downspouts mounted on siding.

consumables.name: Polyurethane sealant for metal-to-substrate junctions
consumables.usage_rate: 1 TUBE per 20 LF of metal-to-wood/masonry joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane caulk for metal-to-wood and metal-to-masonry junctions. Flexible — accommodates differential thermal expansion between metal and adjacent substrates. Paintable after cure (3-7 days). Do NOT use silicone — not paintable. Do NOT use acrylic latex caulk at metal junctions — insufficient flexibility for metal's thermal expansion coefficient.

consumables.name: Half-face respirator with P100/OV cartridges
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per crew member for spray/grinding operations
consumables.notes: Required PPE for spray application (aerosolized coating mist) and power tool grinding (metal dust, rust particles). P100 particulate filter for grinding. OV (organic vapor) cartridge for solvent-based products (DTM alkyd, epoxy, rust converter). Replace cartridges per manufacturer schedule.

consumables.name: Safety glasses (impact-rated ANSI Z87.1)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per crew member
consumables.notes: Required PPE for wire brushing, grinding, and spray operations. Impact-rated per ANSI Z87.1 for wire wheel and grinding disc use. Full seal goggles recommended for overhead grinding.

consumables.name: Heavy work gloves (grinding/wire brushing)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA (pair) per crew member per day of grinding
consumables.notes: Heavy leather or cut-resistant gloves for grinding and wire brushing operations. Metal burrs, sharp edges, and wire brush contact require hand protection beyond standard latex painting gloves.

consumables.name: Tool cleaning solvent (mineral spirits for alkyd, water for acrylic)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 QT per day of alkyd/epoxy product use
consumables.notes: Mineral spirits for alkyd DTM primer and epoxy cleanup. Water cleanup for acrylic DTM products. Epoxy requires solvent cleanup BEFORE cure — cured epoxy cannot be removed from equipment. Budget extra solvent for epoxy pot life waste cleanup.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: Ground area below metal elements (railings, gutters, downspouts) where landscape is adjacent
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Spray overspray from narrow metal profiles drifts 10-15 ft. Cover plantings and mulch beds below and adjacent to railings, gutters, and downspouts. Canvas at base for drips, plastic sheeting for wider overspray zone.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways and driveways below metal elements
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic below work area. Metal paint drips and overspray are especially visible on concrete walkways.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Siding and trim adjacent to gutters, downspouts, and railing mounts
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: LF-based. Masking paper + tape along siding behind gutters and adjacent to downspouts. Critical for spray applications — overspray on siding is highly visible. Brush application reduces but does not eliminate need (drip protection).

ext_window_door_adjacent.description: Windows and doors adjacent to metal elements being painted
ext_window_door_adjacent.notes: Bag or sheet over windows/doors near spray zone. Metal spray mist settles as fine dots on glass — difficult to remove once dried. Mask before spray operations begin.

ext_vehicle_protection.description: Vehicles in driveway or adjacent to work area
ext_vehicle_protection.notes: Full vehicle cover during spray operations. Metal paint overspray on automotive finishes requires compound/polish to remove — prevention is essential. Request vehicles be moved if possible.

compatibility_rules.description: DTM alkyd primer BLOCKED on galvanized substrate — saponification
compatibility_rules.notes: Galvanized steel has zinc oxide coating (alkaline pH ~10-12). Alkyd binder undergoes saponification — alkaline zinc oxide hydrolyzes alkyd ester bonds into soft, sticky soap. Complete coating failure within weeks to months. No remedy except full removal and recoating with compatible system.

compatibility_rules.description: All oil/alkyd finish products BLOCKED on galvanized substrate
compatibility_rules.notes: Same saponification mechanism as COMPAT-METL-001 extends to finish coats. Only water-based acrylic products are compatible with galvanized zinc surface. DTM acrylic finish (SYS_EXT_METL_FINISH_DTM_ACRYLIC) is the correct topcoat.

compatibility_rules.description: DTM alkyd primer BLOCKED on aluminum substrate — flexibility required
compatibility_rules.notes: Aluminum has a high thermal expansion coefficient (2x steel). Alkyd primer becomes brittle over time and cannot accommodate aluminum's thermal movement. Result: cracking, checking, and delamination. Flexible acrylic coatings only on aluminum.

compatibility_rules.description: Aluminum requires flexible acrylic coatings ONLY
compatibility_rules.notes: Aluminum's thermal expansion coefficient (23.1 x 10^-6 /K) is approximately twice that of steel (12 x 10^-6 /K). Coating system must accommodate greater thermal movement. Only flexible acrylic products (DTM acrylic primer, DTM acrylic finish, bonding primer) are suitable.

compatibility_rules.description: Galvanized substrate REQUIRES etch primer or bonding primer
compatibility_rules.selection_logic: bare_galvanized → etch primer; factory_finished_galvanized → bonding primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Slick zinc oxide surface requires either chemical etch (phosphoric acid) or bonding primer adhesion chemistry. Standard DTM acrylic primer will delaminate from untreated galvanized surface within one season.

compatibility_rules.description: Aluminum substrate REQUIRES etch primer or bonding primer
compatibility_rules.selection_logic: bare_aluminum → etch primer; factory_finished_aluminum → bonding primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Aluminum oxide layer is extremely hard and slick — standard primers cannot achieve mechanical adhesion. Etch primer creates micro-profile; bonding primer provides chemical adhesion to intact factory finish.

compatibility_rules.description: Carbon steel and wrought iron REQUIRE ferrous-rated primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Ferrous metals require corrosion-inhibiting primer. DTM acrylic is standard. DTM alkyd for pitted surfaces. Zinc-rich for QT5 critical steel. Epoxy for marginal prep situations. Do NOT use etch primer on ferrous metals — etch primer is for non-ferrous (galvanized, aluminum) only.

compatibility_rules.description: Epoxy primer REQUIRES topcoat within recoat window (24-72 hrs)
compatibility_rules.required_action: Apply DTM acrylic finish within manufacturer's recoat window — typically 24-72 hrs depending on temperature
compatibility_rules.notes: Epoxy has NO UV resistance. Exposed epoxy chalks within days and loses intercoat adhesion after recoat window closes. If window is exceeded, epoxy must be sanded and re-primed. Schedule epoxy prime + topcoat as back-to-back operations — never epoxy prime on Friday with topcoat on Monday.

compatibility_rules.description: Zinc-rich primer restricted to QT5 carbon steel ONLY
compatibility_rules.notes: Zinc-rich primer requires near-white blast cleaning (SSPC-SP10), specialty product knowledge, and careful application technique. Cost and complexity exceed QT3/QT4 scope. Not applicable to galvanized (already zinc-coated), aluminum (no galvanic benefit), or wrought iron (residential wrought iron rarely warrants QT5 zinc-rich).

compatibility_rules.description: Surface rust REQUIRES rust treatment before primer
compatibility_rules.required_action: Mechanical removal (SSPC-SP2/SP3) or chemical conversion (SYS_EXT_METL_RUST_CONVERTER) before any primer application
compatibility_rules.notes: Priming over active rust traps moisture and corrosion products under the coating system. Rust continues progressing under paint, leading to blistering, lifting, and accelerated section loss. All loose rust must be removed. Tight rust on intricate areas may be treated with rust converter.

compatibility_rules.description: Structural rust / section loss is HARD STOP — outside painting scope
compatibility_rules.action: HARD STOP — structural assessment required before painting
compatibility_rules.notes: Structural rust means material section loss — the metal cross-section is reduced. Painting cannot restore structural integrity. Structural elements (railings, columns, beams) with section loss require engineering assessment, potential replacement, or structural repair BEFORE cosmetic coating. Painting over structural rust creates a safety liability — visually conceals a structural deficiency.

risk_notes.topic: Saponification of alkyd products on galvanized steel
risk_notes.risk: Oil-based or alkyd coatings on galvanized zinc surfaces undergo saponification — alkaline zinc oxide hydrolyzes alkyd ester bonds, converting the paint binder into soft, sticky soap. Complete coating system failure within weeks to months. Saponification is irreversible — full removal to bare metal is the only remedy.
risk_notes.mitigation: BLOCK all alkyd/oil-based products on galvanized substrate. Use only water-based acrylic products. Etch primer (SYS_EXT_METL_PRIMER_ETCH) or bonding primer (SYS_EXT_METL_PRIMER_BONDING) as first coat, followed by DTM acrylic finish.

risk_notes.topic: Alkyd brittleness and cracking on aluminum
risk_notes.risk: Aluminum's thermal expansion coefficient is approximately twice that of steel. Alkyd coatings become increasingly brittle as they age (loss of plasticizer). The combination of high thermal movement and brittle coating causes checking, cracking, and delamination — often within 2-3 years.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use flexible acrylic coatings ONLY on aluminum. DTM acrylic primer + DTM acrylic finish. No alkyd, no epoxy (also too rigid for aluminum expansion).

risk_notes.topic: Epoxy UV degradation and recoat window failure
risk_notes.risk: Epoxy primer has excellent chemical resistance and adhesion but ZERO UV resistance. Exposed to sunlight, epoxy chalks within 3-7 days and loses intercoat adhesion after the recoat window closes (24-72 hrs). If the recoat window is missed, the epoxy surface must be sanded and re-primed — adding labor and material cost.
risk_notes.mitigation: Schedule epoxy prime + DTM acrylic topcoat as consecutive operations within the same mobilization. Never prime with epoxy on a Friday expecting to topcoat on Monday (weekend rain/UV exposure can close the window). Verify manufacturer's specific recoat window for the product being used.

risk_notes.topic: Spray overspray on narrow metal profiles
risk_notes.risk: Narrow metal profiles (railings, pickets, downspouts) are small spray targets. Airless spray overspray waste is 25-30% — significantly higher than wall-field spray (10-15%). Overspray drifts 10-15 ft and settles on adjacent siding, windows, vehicles, and landscaping.
risk_notes.mitigation: Budget 25-30% material waste for spray on narrow profiles. Mask all adjacent surfaces thoroughly. Consider brush application for isolated metal elements to eliminate overspray entirely. Wind monitoring — stop spray above 10 mph.

risk_notes.topic: Galvanic corrosion from dissimilar metal contact
risk_notes.risk: Dissimilar metals in contact accelerate galvanic corrosion — the more anodic metal corrodes preferentially. Common residential scenarios: steel fasteners in aluminum gutters, copper flashing against steel framing, galvanized screws in aluminum railing. Coating failure at dissimilar metal junctions exposes the galvanic couple.
risk_notes.mitigation: Identify dissimilar metal contact points during assessment. Isolate with appropriate sealant or dielectric barrier. Ensure primer system covers both metals at junction points. Flag dissimilar metal junctions for extra attention during QA inspection.

risk_notes.risk: Bare steel surfaces (especially after mechanical prep) can develop flash rust within hours in humid conditions (>80% RH). Flash rust under primer compromises adhesion and starts corrosion cycle immediately.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use flash-rust resistant DTM acrylic primer (SYS_EXT_METL_PRIMER_DTM_ACRYLIC) which contains flash-rust inhibitors. Prime same day as mechanical prep — do not leave bare steel overnight. Monitor humidity — if RH >80%, prime immediately after prep or postpone work.

risk_notes.risk: Painting over structurally compromised metal (section loss from rust) visually conceals a safety deficiency. Railings with section loss may appear sound after painting but fail under load. This creates direct safety liability for the painting contractor.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD STOP on structural rust. Document condition with photos. Require structural assessment and repair/replacement before coating. Do not paint metal with visible section loss. See COMPAT-METL-011.

risk_notes.topic: Lead paint hazard on pre-1978 metal surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Metal surfaces on pre-1978 homes frequently contain lead-based paint — especially railings, gutters, and ornamental iron. Wire brushing and grinding lead paint generates hazardous dust requiring EPA RRP Rule compliance.
risk_notes.mitigation: Test for lead on all pre-1978 metal surfaces before mechanical prep. If positive: RRP-certified firm, containment, HEPA vacuum, wet methods. Lead-safe work practices add significant cost and time. Budget accordingly.

material_quantity_notes.lf_to_sf_conversion: Metal items are measured in LF or EA but coverage rates are SF/gal. Conversion factors: Railing ~1.5 SF/LF (both sides pickets + rails), Gutter ~0.75 SF/LF (exterior face), Downspout ~0.4 SF/LF (circumference). Ornamental iron: estimate SF per piece based on profile.
material_quantity_notes.spray_waste_on_narrow_profiles: Spray on narrow metal profiles wastes 25-30% material from overspray missing the target. This is significantly higher than wall-field spray waste (10-15%). Budget spray modifier of 1.25-1.30x on all coverage calculations for spray-applied metal work.
material_quantity_notes.coat_count_standard: Primer: 1 coat (all systems). Finish: 2 coats at all quality tiers (QT3-QT5). Metal requires two finish coats to achieve holiday-free coverage on convex profiles — single coat leaves thin spots on curves and edges.
material_quantity_notes.rust_converter_partial_area: Rust converter is applied only to rusted areas, not full surface. Estimate rust-affected area as a percentage of total surface. Light rust (<25% area): 0.25x total SF. Moderate rust (25-50%): 0.50x. Heavy surface rust (>50%): full area.
material_quantity_notes.primer_system_stacking: Some conditions require two primer layers: etch primer + DTM acrylic on bare galvanized/aluminum for best adhesion build. Etch primer provides adhesion profile, DTM acrylic provides barrier protection. Budget both primer materials when stacking.
material_quantity_notes.epoxy_pot_life_waste: Two-component epoxy primer has limited pot life (4-8 hrs). Unused mixed material at end of pot life is waste. For small metal jobs, pot life waste can be 10-20% of mixed material. Mix only what can be applied within pot life window.

assumptions.value: 350-500 SF/gal depending on surface condition and profile
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md §4; manufacturer PDS data (SW Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic)
assumptions.note: Coverage range is wide due to metal profile variation — smooth flat steel at high end, pitted ornamental iron at low end. Midpoint 400 SF/gal used for standard estimation.

assumptions.value: Railing 1.5 SF/LF, Gutter 0.75 SF/LF, Downspout 0.4 SF/LF
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not specify LF-to-SF conversion factors for metal profiles. Values derived from typical residential profile dimensions. Railing factor includes both sides of pickets at standard 4-inch spacing plus top and bottom rails. Gutter and downspout factors for standard 5-inch K-style gutter and 2x3 rectangular downspout. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: 25-30% material waste from overspray on narrow targets
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms significant overspray on small targets. 25-30% waste is consistent with field experience on railings and downspouts. Smaller targets (individual pickets) may exceed 30%.

assumptions.value: 0.3-0.5 mils DFT (much thinner than DTM primers at 2-4 mils)
assumptions.note: Etch primer acts as adhesion promoter, not barrier coat. Very thin film — high coverage per gallon but provides no standalone protection. Must be topcoated.

assumptions.value: 2 finish coats at all quality tiers (QT3-QT5)
assumptions.note: Metal's convex profiles (round pickets, curved gutters) cause single-coat holidays on the sides of curved surfaces. Two coats ensure continuous film build on all surfaces. This is a physical requirement, not a quality preference — even QT3 needs two coats on metal.

assumptions.value: Stainless steel bristles required for wire brushing galvanized and aluminum
assumptions.note: Carbon steel wire brush bristles leave iron deposits embedded in galvanized/aluminum surfaces. These iron deposits create galvanic corrosion cells, causing premature rust spots on non-ferrous substrates. Stainless steel bristles are electrochemically neutral.

uncertainty_flags.description: Conversion factors for railing, gutter, and downspout LF-to-SF are based on typical residential profiles but actual dimensions vary. Standard 5-inch K-style gutter vs 6-inch half-round vs box gutter have significantly different surface areas per LF.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material estimates could be off by 15-25% for non-standard profiles. Ornamental iron is especially variable — no standard profile exists.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: PaintScope input for metal profile type (standard/wide/ornamental) with profile-specific SF/LF lookup. Or: optional SF override input for estimator to enter measured SF directly.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Zinc-rich primer applicability in residential scope
uncertainty_flags.description: Zinc-rich primer (SYS_EXT_METL_PRIMER_ZINC_RICH) requires near-white blast cleaning (SSPC-SP10) which is rarely available in residential painting scope. Included at QT5 for completeness but may be impractical for most residential metal projects.
uncertainty_flags.impact: QT5 metal spec may promise zinc-rich corrosion protection that cannot be delivered without specialty subcontractor for blast cleaning.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Determine if QT5 metal scope should include blast cleaning as a subcontracted prep item, or if zinc-rich should be limited to specialty/commercial scope only.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Epoxy primer pot life waste quantification
uncertainty_flags.description: Two-component epoxy primer waste from expired pot life is estimated at 10-20% on small metal jobs but actual waste depends on job size, temperature (shorter pot life in heat), and crew efficiency.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material cost for epoxy primer may be underestimated on small jobs or hot-weather work. A 1-gallon mix with 20% waste costs the same as a full gallon.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field data on actual epoxy pot life waste rates by job size and temperature range.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Lead paint prevalence on pre-1978 metal surfaces
uncertainty_flags.description: Lead paint testing and RRP compliance costs are not modeled in this materials specification. Pre-1978 metal surfaces have high probability of lead-based paint, especially ornamental iron and railings that were painted with lead-based enamel for durability.
uncertainty_flags.impact: RRP compliance on lead-positive metal adds significant cost (containment, HEPA, disposal, certified labor) that is not captured in standard material/consumable budgets.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Lead assessment flag as required PaintScope input for pre-1978 homes. RRP cost adder as a modifier when lead is confirmed.
